turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on through. You look like you'd rather be somewhere else.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, look, it's hardly worth coming in. Bit of a guts ache after a wedding, that's all.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): When was the wedding?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Saturday, my cousin's, up in Geelong. Seafood platter. The band was shocking, but that's another story.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Since Saturday, what have the symptoms actually been?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): The runs, mostly. Watery. I chucked up a few times as well, but that's done. Honestly it's nothing.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many times have you opened your bowels?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Um. Yesterday was the bad one. Six, maybe seven. Wasn't counting, could've been eight. Today only about three, so it's easing.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood in it, or black stool?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Nah. No blood, not black. Just brown water. Gross, I know.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tell me about the vomiting.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Started Sunday morning. Twice on Sunday, once Monday arvo, nothing since. Kept breakfast down, no worries.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or chills?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Don't think so. Haven't checked or anything. Just a bit washed out.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anyone else from the wedding been crook?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): My brother, his missus, two of the groomsmen. All on the seafood. So it's obviously just a dodgy feed.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you keeping fluids down?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Water sits a bit funny, but it stays down. Not drinking heaps. Had a tea this morning. Traffic on the ring road was worse than the guts, tell you what.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dizziness when you stand? Dry mouth? Weeing less?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Mouth's dry, I'll admit that. Weeing a bit less, still going. No dizziness. I'm not dehydrated.

[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll have a look: pulse is one hundred and two, blood pressure one eighteen over seventy four, temp thirty seven point two. Tongue's dry, and the skin on your forearm springs back normally.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): There you go. Nothing to write home about.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse is up and your mouth's dry, so there is mild dehydration, even if you feel okay.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): If you say so. I drove here fine.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): What have you taken for the diarrhoea?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Little green capsules from the chemist. Imodium, the stop-you-up ones. Two yesterday, two this morning.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Two milligrams each?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Yep, two mg on the packet. Chemist said don't, if it's a bug just let it run. I took them anyway. Had a shift at the warehouse.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any tablets you take all the time?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Blood pressure one. Little white tablet in the mornings.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Name and dose?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Perindopril. Five milligrams. Been on it a couple of years, something like that.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything you've stopped?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Purple capsule for heartburn, binned it months ago. Can't remember the real name — Nexium, maybe, or not. Doesn't matter, I don't take it.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines, or anything else?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing. Never have.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Other illnesses, or operations?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Blood pressure, that's it. Appendix out when I was about ten. And last year the GP did bloods and said the kidney number was borderline. She wasn't fussed, so I'm not.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which test, and what was the actual result?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No clue. Just borderline. Might've been creatinine. She didn't repeat it.

[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll summarise: diarrhoea since Saturday after the wedding seafood, about six to eight watery motions yesterday and about three today, vomiting settled since Monday, and several others from that meal are unwell. Dry mouth, less urine, pulse one hundred and two, and no blood, no black stool, no dizziness, no fever you've noticed. Perindopril five milligrams each morning, plus Imodium two milligrams, two capsules yesterday and two today, against the chemist's advice. A blood test last year was called borderline for the kidneys, with no figure.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, that's the lot. Nearly didn't bother you with it.

[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): I think this is most likely foodborne gastroenteritis, with mild dehydration. Please stop the Imodium and let it clear. Drink little and often, Gastrolyte if you can get it, otherwise water. A stool test only if it's still bad in a couple of days, or you can't keep fluids down, or you see blood, not one today.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): A stool test is a bit much. I'll drink and I'll lay off the green capsules.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back straight away if you feel faint, if you stop weeing, or if the vomiting comes back hard. If it's not settling by Friday, ring and we'll fit you in.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. Friday if I have to. Thanks.

omissions.text: Patient had kept breakfast down and was able to keep fluids down despite water 'sitting a bit funny'.
Several specific contacts from the wedding were also unwell after eating the seafood: the patient's brother, his wife, and two groomsmen.
The patient reported reduced oral intake: 'not drinking heaps' and had only had a tea that morning.
Negative finding nuance is recorded too strongly: for fever/chills the patient said 'Don't think so' and had not checked, rather than a definite absence of fever/chills.
Past history included a prior GP comment that the 'kidney number' was borderline last year and may have been creatinine, with no repeat test done.
